subject: sinking city
title: What If a City Sank Half a Metre Every Year? Mexico City Is, and It Can't Stop

scenes.text: What if a city of 21 million sank half a metre a year? One is. It can't stop.
Mexico City sits on the bed of an ancient lake: 100 metres of soft, wet clay. The Aztecs built their capital on an island in it.
Over 70 percent of its drinking water is pumped from underground. As the water goes, the clay grains pack tighter.
In the 1900s it sank 9 centimetres a year. Today, in places, almost 50. Pavements split, buildings tilt, pipes crack.
Scientists used 115 years of surveys and 24 years of satellite radar. The clay is 17 percent compressed. It can reach 30.
That means up to 30 more metres of sinking over 150 years. Stop every pump tomorrow, and the ground keeps going down.

description:
What if a city sank half a metre a year? Parts of Mexico City are, and a 2021 study in the Journal of Geophysical Research found the sinking cannot be reversed.
The city sits on the clay bed of ancient Lake Texcoco. Decades of pumping groundwater, which supplies over 70 percent of its drinking water, have let the clay compact. The rate has climbed from about 9 centimetres a year in the early 1900s to nearly 50 today, and the clay could sink up to 30 metres more over the next 150 years, cracking buildings, sewers and water lines.
What should we run through next?
first_comment: The cracks also let polluted surface water seep into the aquifer the city drinks from, so the sinking and the water shortage feed each other. Which city should we run through next?
